subject: Sage Health: model-fit & context plan for onboarding pilot
messages:
From: Carlos Mejia <carlos@sagehealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sage Health Engineering <eng@sagehealth.com>
Date: 2025-09-30T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: model shortlist & traffic snapshot for Q4 pilot

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the quick intro call this morning. We want to move the pilot forward for the clinical-chat assistant: goal is to validate answer quality and latency at ~P95 for clinician queries. A few quick facts from our side to help model selection: 

- Pilot scope: 200 clinicians, anticipated 6-week pilot starting mid-Oct.
- Expected concurrency: peak 25 concurrent sessions (web UI), average 6 QPS; expected burst patterns around shift changes (06:00, 14:00, 22:00).
- Typical prompt: triage + chart context: ~350 tokens prompt on average, some longer threads up to 2,000 tokens.
- Expected daily tokens (rough): 200 clinicians * ~40 prompts/day * ~450 tokens = ~3.6M tokens/day (ballpark).
- Data sensitivity: some PHI; we will need Private deployment scoping and SOC2 evidence.

Can you share an initial model shortlist and guidance on context-window tradeoffs (latency vs. cost)? Also attaching a short example payloads file so you can see real prompt shapes.

Carlos
Carlos Mejia
Head of Clinical Integrations, Sage Health
Attachment: example_payloads.json (stub)
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-30T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: model shortlist & traffic snapshot for Q4 pilot

Carlos —

Appreciate the detail, that helps a lot. Attached is a mutual_action_plan.xlsx with proposed milestones. Initial thoughts on model fit and context-length strategy below, high-level:

1) Model shortlist (candidates for pilot) — two lanes: low-latency vs. high-quality:
   - Redwood-OPT-13B-q4 (low-latency, quantized): favors sub-200ms token latency on dedicated pools, good for tighter SLAs.
   - OpenMed-Large-30B (high-quality, 32k context): best on longer chart-context but higher cost.
   - Redwood-Constellation-7B (sparser, cheaper) for routing low-context prompts or recall-only paths.

2) Context handling recommendations:
   - Primary: prefix caching + selective summarization for chart history. Keep active context to ~2-4k tokens for most queries.
   - Extended-context mode: for occasional long threads, route to OpenMed-30B with 32k window; fall back to summarization if latency-bound.

3) Token volume estimate: based on your 3.6M/day number, with a 70/30 split between short and long contexts, projected cost profile attached in sage_token_profile.csv.

Next steps: Jordan will scope the Dedicated pool sizing and rough QPS to GPU mapping; Ben will outline rollout timing and billing milestones. If the numbers look reasonable we'll send a short statement of work + DocuSign for the MAP.

Thanks — can you confirm whether you prefer Private (VPC) or Redwood Dedicated for the pilot (if PHI is in scope we typically recommend Private)?

—Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (stub)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-01T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: model shortlist & traffic snapshot for Q4 pilot

Quick technical notes from infra/serving perspective:

- Sizing: for 6 average QPS (6 sustained) and 25 peak concurrent sessions we recommend starting with a 4-GPU dedicated pool (A40/A100 class equiv) if using Redwood-OPT-13B-q4. That supports autoscale headroom for bursts; we can autoscale to 6-8 GPUs for day-of peaks.

- For OpenMed-30B (32k): memory and kv-cache pressure increase. Expect ~2.5x token compute cost compared to 13B. We can run mixed routing: short queries to 13B, long-context to OpenMed-30B.

- Batching & latency: enable continuous batching with max-latency 50ms to keep per-token latency predictable. Prefix KV caching for patient chart snippets will save ~25-35% token compute on repeat queries (useful for follow-ups).

- Embeddings: if you plan to do similarity search for chart retrieval, estimate ~1 embedding per patient update and 1 per search; embedding QPS negligible relative to generation but storage/IO matters.

Attaching a short model_candidates.pdf with perf numbers from our test harness.

Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: model_candidates.pdf (perf summary)
From: Carlos Mejia <carlos@sagehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-02T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: model shortlist & traffic snapshot for Q4 pilot

Thanks Jordan — super helpful. A few clarifications from our infra team:

- Our compliance team strongly prefers Private deployment (VPC) for PHI.
- Confirmed pilot numbers: worst-case daily active prompts could be 9,600 (200 clinicians * 48 prompts), so peak day tokens could reach ~4.3M if we see longer prompts.
- Embeddings: we'll run nightly index updates (~10k embeddings/day) and a search QPS of ~2-4 during clinic hours.

I attached the example_payloads.json showing the longer-case prompts (some push to ~1,800 tokens).

If OpenMed-30B is going to increase costs by 2.5x, would you recommend doing an adaptive routing test instead of keeping it default for all long prompts?

Carlos

Carlos / team —

Thanks for the numbers and the payloads. Based on the worst-case tokens and compliance requirement for PHI we recommend the following pilot configuration: 

- Deployment: Redwood Private (VPC) — we'll open the Private deployment intake and SOC2 checklist.
- Routing policy: adaptive routing by estimated effective context length:
   * If estimated context <= 4k tokens route to Redwood-OPT-13B-q4 (default).
   * If estimated context > 4k tokens (long chart-heavy prompts) or when clinician marks "full chart" route to OpenMed-30B (32k).
   * Fallback: summarization path to keep latency under P95 target when OpenMed is at capacity.

- Pilot model shortlist (final two): Redwood-OPT-13B-q4 and OpenMed-Large-30B (we will run routing test and A/B quality evals).

- Preliminary token estimate (worst-case day): 4.3M gen tokens/day + 10k embeddings/night. With adaptive routing we estimate cost delta vs. OpenMed-only to be ~40% lower (detailed numbers in sage_token_profile.csv).

- Timeline: finalize MAP and SOW this week -> Private intake and infra procurement next week -> pilot environment up by Oct 20 -> pilot start Oct 27.

Action items for Sage Health:
1) Confirm Private deployment approval and sign the MAP (DocuSign link sent separately).
2) Approve sample payloads and mark any additional PHI classes.
3) Share any additional throughput scenarios (weekend/holiday spikes).

I'll loop solutions engineering in for the intake call once the MAP is signed.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | monica_patel@redwood.com
